reviews.title: How to slowly ruin an app, and then accelerate
reviews.text:
What used to be a reliable and well engineered app is now unreliable (eg no
longer good at recognising labels, terrible at entering locations where you consumed wine) and takes many more clicks to do the routine tasks like entering a bottle you have drunk at a restaurant. 
The designers seem confused about their aims - is it a platform to buy wine? Is it a review site? Is it to manage your wine collection? 
And the introduction of AI is a truly spectacular fail - to be told I am drinking my first French cab sauvignon when there are hundreds of bottles of it in my Vivino records… and it seems now to get the grapes wrong in the wine descriptions quite often. 
A shame. 
Guess Cellar Tracker must be rejoicing.

PS the woeful (AI) reply to the review tells you everything you need to know about the company’s attitude to customers and actually fixing anything.


And now, the app will not let me log in, and insists I set up a new ID. It’s time to depart

reviews.title: No manual wine entry
reviews.text: This might’ve been a feature previously, but there’s no way to just take a picture of a wine and enter your information manually. You have to get matched with online wines for some reason. And that’s a huge pain in the butt when you buy locally produced short run or even not even nationally sold wines just from a local tiny vineyard. What a waste this app used to be nice. I don’t want wine recommendations I don’t wanna be matched online, I just wanna keep a record of things that I’ve bought and tasted for my own reference.

reviews.title: Poor execution
reviews.text:
Great to have a wine enthusiast app. Unfortunately this is a very poorly executed one. Wine classification, region and style identification , filtering, basically all functionalities are subpar. It is not on a level to justify a premium membership. And when are they going to fix the bugs? Too many to list, but for starters, when you chose to display your wines from a particular grape of region, why do you get everything that you scanned? Who and how gives app choice awards?
Getting worse and buggier with each iteration.

reviews.title: Very good app, difficult wine delivery
reviews.text:
I enjoy the app, especially the different components of the wine identified as a graph.  My wife and I determined our taste profiles by looking at the profiles of wine we preferred, and often use the profile in identifying new wines to try.
Purchasing has proven to be difficult.  The deals on wines that I have purchased in the past are very good.  The expected delivery times are so wide I have not ordered wine because I was not sure I would be available for pickup under worse case delivery window.  My last order I had delivered to an address, and supplier would not allow hold at shipper’s location.   
I am ordering this only because the discount is World of Wines.  I know with this vendor if I need to hold the wine I can do it, unlike my last order when I decided to stop ordering from Vivino.

reviews.title: My 10yr cellar now hidden behind paywall, can’t trust the app anymore
reviews.text: I’ve been a user for over a decade. Have 100+ bottles in the cellar and almost 2k reviews. When Vivino first introduced a paid version a few years ago it hid useful and formerly free features behind a paywall. Today I just discovered that I have been blocked from adding any new bottles to my cellar without becoming a premium subscriber. This is extortion. I placed my trust in this app and this company to keep my data safe and accessible for over a decade, and then they effectively block me from managing my cellar in the app. For shame, Vivino. You have let greed spoil what was once a great app, and are harming your longest standing users. Truly disappointing. I will have to look for alternatives unless this cap on cellar size is removed (or for heavens sake, set it higher than a measly 20 bottles… your most engaged users will all have more than 20 bottles in the cellar and the cellar feature keeps them coming back to your app regularly which is a flywheel that drives engagement and product metrics for you… this isn’t just breaking user trust, it’s a poor product and business decision to boot).

reviews.title: Recent update is terrible
reviews.text:
Most recent update of the app is a big step back. One of the main reasons I use the app is keep track of my own ratings. Suddenly, I can’t see that anymore. I also doesn’t show how many wines you’ve had of a particular style. Key question…what’s the point of the app now?!

I’m all for new features, but why do they have to come at the expense of the most useful parts of this app?

Really hoping they’ll roll back these terrible changes, but cancelled my membership in the meantime. Convenient it was due for renewal next week.

reviews.title: Getting worse and worse
reviews.text:
I’ve had this app for years and used to absolutely love it but it’s got worse and worse over the years and I barely bother any more.

There’s been various attempts to monetise the app more
Effectively, but this isn’t even the problem. It’s now extremely difficult to even get to your old reviews after you’ve scanned a wine - to me this is one of the fundamental purposes of the app. 

Still ok to access community scores I guess but nothing like as good as it used to be.

reviews.title: Delivery and customer service
reviews.text:
I placed an order which was going to the wrong address, I contacted Vivino promptly. To be told nothing they could do, I then waited 4 days for order to be dispatched and told I can change address at that point. When I tried to do the carrier said only Vivino can change delivery address. I went back to customer service again and explained this. To be told they had sorted it, and it would be delivered to my home address. It was delivered to my old work instead. 
I have been asking to speak to a customer service manager , and told they will be in touch shortly. 5 days and still waiting . 
Shocking customer service when things go wrong.

reviews.title: Extremely difficult to get help
reviews.text:
I bought a dozen bottles of Caymus. I selected the yellow labeled bottle (usually $80-$90/bottle retail) that showed $37 if 12 bought. I knew that was almost too good to be true & that's what our ended up being. 12 bottles of the brown label Caymus ($50-$55 retail) showed up. It was an absolute bait & switch. Never did it reflect the brown labeled bottle during my purchase, but street using the chat to get support, they changed/updated the app so if you clicked on the yellow label to purchase, it showed a split screen with the brown labeled bottle. 
Their proposed solution was for me to ship all 12 bottles back for a refund - and I guarantee you that would not have included my expense to ship them back. I no longer trust this site to order wine or to resolve a fraudulent situation in a satisfactory manner.
Lastly, the app is not intuitive and won't easily allow me to cancel my $4.99/mo membership.  The support is chat only and are no longer supporting voice Support - so support is horrible.
